what: Packaged stack with Dex, oauth2-proxy and an nginx gateway in front of the console and case API, and the PostgreSQL case store
hardware: Apple M3 Pro, 11 cores, macOS; Docker Desktop engine 29.5.3; all services and checks on one machine, loopback only
compose_project: p09idcheck (disposable; removed with its volumes afterwards)

first_attempt.result: identity check 21/22; the stack browser run stopped at its first page load; the gateway header check 1/7
causes: nginx turned the relative sign-in redirect into http://127.0.0.1/oauth2/start (port 80, the container's own port). Fixed with absolute_redirect off.
oauth2-proxy's default approval_prompt=force made Dex show a consent screen on every sign-in. Fixed with --approval-prompt=auto.
The header check started sending requests while its stand-in upstream was still starting (502s). Its readiness wait now requires the stand-in's 401.
first_attempt.after_fixes: The stack was removed with its volumes and every check rerun from a fresh start; the counts above are from that rerun.

case_database.payguard_cases_role_connect_to_ledger_db: refused: permission denied for database "payguard" (no CONNECT privilege)

schema_race_4_openers_on_fresh_db.without_advisory_lock_raw_create_if_not_: 10 of 10 repeats raised UniqueViolation in 3 of 4 openers

case_database.opt_in_postgres_tests: 3 passed (reopen durability, concurrent review, concurrent first open) against payguard_cases_it on the stack's PostgreSQL

authorization_smoke.command: docker compose -p p09idcheck ... --profile simulate run --rm simulator (report written inside the container, so bench/burst_results.json was not overwritten)
authorization_smoke.decisions: 1 APPROVED by rules fallback (first call after a cold start), 7 DECLINED by MODEL_DECLINE at score 1.0
authorization_smoke.case_path: Kafka -> cases-worker -> PostgreSQL opened 7 cases for the burst; the simulator signed in as analyst@payguard.local with Dex's password grant and drafted case_auth_demo_2b088f6ebe_7 through the gateway (rules_fallback draft, 8 citations, drafted_by analyst@payguard.local)

limits: Synthetic data only. Demo users and secrets are public local-demo-only placeholders; plain HTTP on loopback, cookie not marked secure.
One cases-api process; the gateway race used its thread pool. The two-store race is covered by the opt-in PostgreSQL test.
No load test was run with the PostgreSQL case store; the 22 October CPU and saturation figures used the SQLite case store.
Audit retention is still a seven-year placeholder, not an agreed policy.
